title: Dispatch: opus:F-09 legacy-row generalization (attempt 2)
description:
Implement docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md §8 step 3 ("Generalization PR(s): re-derive and migrate the remaining legacy rows under R0"). **Read the whole design first** (esp. §1 reading of F-09, R0, R1, R2, R4, R5, invariants §4) — it is the authority. The vertical slice (PR #594, merged b9f4fa9e; child bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.1 — read its notes) established the pattern: RULE_ADJUDICATION_CONTEXT (src/rules/ruleAdjudicationContext.ts), RULE_KNOWN_LIMITS (src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts), capability ledger data rows (src/rules/deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts, CONTRACT UNCHANGED), and materializeEngineProcedureCoverage in packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/ruleDispositions.ts projecting those runtime datasets into the audit coverage rows (with runtimeSource identity).

Worktree/branch: .worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.4.1 on branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.4.1, cut from integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.4 (== origin/main 7452fbff). Install with `npm ci` first.

## Scope (membership by query, not by count)
Every key in UNBOUND_ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE whose status is NOT 'implemented' — i.e. model-adjudicated-supported, partial, design-blocked, including rows with externalClauses. Enumerate with a script over the module, not by hand. (Snapshot at 7452fbff for orientation only: ~106 model-adjudicated-supported, 14 partial, 9 design-blocked, 4 of them with externalClauses. Never write these numbers into a test.) The 41 'implemented' rows are OUT of scope, except where a row you re-derive turns out to be implemented now (then treat it like rule:long-rest in the slice: status implemented with real runtimeOwner + existing evidence test files, key added to IMPLEMENTED_ROWS_WITHOUT_SELECTED_CAPABILITY, NO binding). If you notice a stale 'implemented' row, file a follow-up bead; do not fix it here.

**End state:** UNBOUND_ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE contains only 'implemented' rows; every other coverage row is projected from a runtime dataset. Enforce that in materializeEngineProcedureCoverage (throw if an authored unbound row has any other status) so the single-definition rule is structural. The ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE key set must be unchanged.

## Per-row R0 procedure (every row, no mechanical copying)
1. Read the rule record's source text in packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json.
2. Re-derive the legacy claim against the CURRENT runtime: grep the named tools/state modules, check DEFAULT_TOOLS (orchestrator/toolRegistry), `bd show` any named bead (closed beads frequently make partial/unimplemented claims stale — rule:long-rest was).
3. Assign exactly one R0 outcome — confirmed / rewritten / retired — and write a code comment beside the dataset entry: `// R0 <outcome>: <one-line evidence: code path, test, or bead>` (same style as the slice entries).
4. Write the entry:
   - adjudication context -> RULE_ADJUDICATION_CONTEXT { tools, dmContext }. `tools` = registered tools the DM actually uses for this rule (validated by validateRuleAdjudicationContext); `lookup_rules` normally included.
   - known limit -> RULE_KNOWN_LIMITS { limit: partial|unimplemented|deferred, statement, findingId, externalClauses? , designOwner? }. design-blocked -> 'deferred', statement written from ADR 0018 (docs/adr/0018-*) where the block is the single-class/character-scope decision; read each designOwner bead to write a truthful statement; designOwner stays as history only.
   - A row may land in BOTH channels (design R4: residual adjudication + a known limit coexist) — see materializer decision below. A retired legacy claim is REPLACED by the correct re-derived statement; every engine-procedure row still ends in at least one channel (or implemented). If a row genuinely has nothing true to say in any channel, stop on that row and record it on this bead as a question; do not invent text.
   - externalClauses: re-derive each clause (is the owning bead closed? does the pack/runtime now carry it? — rule:charges' clause was retired in the slice this way). Keep only surviving clauses.
   - findingId: keep the id the materializer currently assigns (readiness-integrity for partial/unimplemented, engine-capability-ownership for design-blocked, rule-corpus-procedures default for external clauses) unless re-derivation shows a different registered finding owns it; ids are validated by validateRuleKnownLimits.
5. **Model-facing text** (dmContext / statement): written for the DM at the table, reviewed against the source record, 1-3 sentences, tool names exact. NEVER expose legacy shorthand or internal identifiers: no "F1-F10", "D1/D2", hook names, bead ids, "engine-procedure", file paths, or a verbatim legacy contextRequirement/missing note. Never claim the rule is supported/safe/fully enforced; say what Eshyra does and what the DM must do. Absence of a channel is never a claim (invariant 3).

## Materializer decision (supervisor, already made)
Extend materializeEngineProcedureCoverage so one key may appear in both RULE_ADJUDICATION_CONTEXT and RULE_KNOWN_LIMITS: the audit row's status comes from the limit (KNOWN_LIMIT_AUDIT_STATUS), `primitives`/`contextRequirement` come from the context, `missing`/findingId/externalClauses/designOwner from the limit, and the identity proof covers BOTH runtime entries (e.g. runtimeSource as the limit plus a second identity field for the context, or a { adjudicationContext, knownLimit } object — your call, keep the existing slice identity assertions passing). Keep the one-limit-per-key restriction (merge two limits into one statement if needed). Add a permanent test for the both-channels projection. The facade (ruleAwareness.ts) and ledger contract are unchanged — they already support any combination.

## Tests
- Do not weaken assertions. Tests in ruleDispositions.test.ts / other files that pin a legacy row's fields may follow the data to the runtime dataset (same claim, new reading path) or change where R0 changed the claim — each such change must cite the R0 evidence in the commit/notes. Tests elsewhere that import ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE (usageCounters, actionEconomy, hpLifecycle, activeEffects, inspiration, attunement tests) must keep passing.
- No corpus-wide completeness test (ADR 0020; design §5). The validators (tool names, findingIds) already run over every entry; the structural "only implemented rows are authored in the audit script" check lives in the materializer.
- Discovery probe / intervention suites (test/discovery/*) must stay green WITHOUT retuning any budget: many more rule records now carry statements into the packet. If packet size displaces must-consider material, STOP and record it on this bead.

## Disjointness (hard constraint)
A sibling dispatch is concurrently implementing condition relationships. Do NOT modify: packages/core/src/rules/recordRelationships.ts, src/rules/packLoader.ts, src/discovery/expansion.ts, anything under packages/core/scripts/importers/, packages/core/data/rules-packs/, packages/core/test/rules/recordRelationships.test.ts, packages/core/test/rules/conditionRelationships.test.ts, docs/inventories/*, docs/design/*. If one must change, stop and record why.

## Completion report (bd update --append-notes)
R0 outcome tally by outcome and channel (computed, from a script); every RETIRED claim and every row that changed channel or status vs legacy, each with its evidence; rows that landed in both channels; externalClauses kept/retired; any row you stopped on. Follow-ups via bd create (parent eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4).

# ATTEMPT 2 — read this section first; it overrides anything above it conflicts with

Worktree/branch for THIS attempt: .worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.4.2 on branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.4.2 (cut from eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.4 == origin/main 7452fbff).

Attempt 1 (bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.4.1, commit 88764af8) was REJECTED in supervisor review. Read its bead notes. You may read that commit (`git show 88764af8`) as an UNTRUSTED DRAFT: its materializer/test changes may be reused after you review them, but no data entry may be copied without doing the per-row work below. Why it was rejected, and the hard rules that follow:

1. **Row-specific R0 evidence.** Every entry's comment `// R0 <outcome>: <evidence>` must name evidence specific to THAT row: the module/function that does or does not implement the clause (path + symbol), a specific closed bead id, or a specific test that exercises that behavior. `packages/core/test/ruleAwareness.test.ts` is NOT evidence for any row. For a pure-adjudication row with no runtime owner, name the source clause that requires judgment and the specific tool/state module the DM uses (or that none exists) — not a generic phrase.
2. **Row-specific dmContext.** Each dmContext must say what the DM decides for THIS rule and what state, if any, the DM records with which tool. Forbidden: any sentence template reused across entries (attempt 1 had 73 copies of "Use lookup_rules to consult X. The DM applies the rule to the current scene…"). Before committing, run a script that splits every dmContext/statement into sentences and prints any sentence (after replacing the rule's own name) shared by more than 2 entries; fix every hit. Put the script's clean output in your completion notes. Do not tell the DM to "use roll for state changes"; roll only rolls dice.
3. **Minimal, justified tools.** Do NOT copy the legacy `primitives` list. List only tools the DM would actually call for this rule. Every tool other than `lookup_rules` must be named in that entry's dmContext. Enforce this as a check in `validateRuleAdjudicationContext` (permanent: it is the channel's contract that its tool list is what its context tells the DM to use). The three slice entries (cover, opportunity-attacks, charges) already satisfy it — verify.
4. **Single owner modules.** Entries live directly in `src/rules/ruleAdjudicationContext.ts` and `src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts` — no `*Generalized.ts` side files and no object spread merging.
5. **Do not rewrite already-approved slice text** (cover, opportunity-attacks, charges, suffocating, channel-divinity); it passed review in PR #594.
6. **ADR 0018 multiclass rows** (class-features, extra-attack, hit-points-and-hit-dice, multiclassing, multiclassing-proficiency-bonus, spellcasting, unarmored-defense — these records are the Multiclassing chapter's subsections; confirm from their text): `deferred`, each statement written for that row, modeled on the approved channel-divinity statement ("Eshyra supports single-class characters only under ADR 0018. A character with more than one class is refused, so this multiclass <specific interaction> is deliberately unsupported and is not adjudicated."). Name the specific interaction per row. Never tell the DM to refuse a character. `rule:experience-points` is also that chapter's multiclass XP subsection ("cleric 6/fighter 1…"): supervisor decision — treat it as `deferred` with the same pattern, NOT implemented (single-class satisfaction is trivial, not an implementation of the multiclass rule).
7. **Leads from attempt 1 that the supervisor spot-checked** (still re-derive and cite): rule:feats → implemented (levelUpEngine.ts featsGained / feat-in-place-of-ASI path; find its real test); rule:customizing-a-background → implemented (characterDraft.ts BackgroundCustomization / applyBackgroundCustomization; find its real test); rule:armor-guidance → partial known limit, evidence packages/core/src/character/derivedValues.ts header ("armor class / attack bonuses — need equipment (eshyra-b69j.13)") — check eshyra-b69j.13's status.
8. **Honest tally.** The completion report's confirmed/rewritten/retired tally must be computed from the R0 comments by a script, and you must list every `rewritten` and `retired` row with its one-line reason. "Confirmed" means the legacy claim held as-is after checking; if you changed the claim's substance, it is `rewritten`.

Quality over speed: this is ~129 rows of individual judgment. Work through them in source-chapter order, and commit only when every row meets rules 1-3.
